basis: Cutaneous and gastrointestinal venous malformations define disease; coagulation abnormalities occur in 30-79%, with prolonged bleeding time in 80-99%.
Arterial calcification and occlusion with periarticular calcification and early arthritis define the disease.
Malignant smooth-muscle tumour arising in the anus.
Congenital patellar displacement with knee deformity, contracture and impaired extension.
CD27 immunodeficiency with lymphoproliferation and splenic involvement; hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic injury.
Circumscribed disseminated keratosis denotes a cutaneous keratinization disorder; no additional organ involvement is established.
N-glycosylation disorder defined by developmental impairment and immunodeficiency; coagulation cascade abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
Inherited erythroid marrow disorder: refractory sideroblastic anemia is reported in 20/20, supporting blood involvement beyond leukemia susceptibility.
Testicular germ-cell malignancy arises in a reproductive organ; no endocrine dysfunction is established.
Dry socket affects the oral extraction socket and exposed alveolar bone after clot loss; infection is not intrinsic to the condition.
Disorder affecting multiple spinal nerve roots.
Progressive palmoplantar keratinization and nail disease; finger flexion contractures cause locomotor impairment in 30-79%.
Polydactyly defines disease; neurodevelopmental impairment 50-100%, ocular defects 1/2 and ASD 1/1; renal agenesis 1/3 omitted by cap. Samples are small.
Paralytic failure of eyelid closure defines this eyelid disorder; an underlying facial neuropathy is a separate condition.
Persistent idiopathic facial pain is a neurologic pain disorder; no direct oral tissue injury is established.
Congenital ataxia, hypotonia and nystagmus define neurologic and ocular dysfunction; abnormal auditory brainstem responses alone do not establish ear damage.
Unequal refractive power of the two eyes.
Benign cutaneous hair-follicle hamartoma.
KLHL24-related skin fragility, scarring and hair loss; dilated cardiomyopathy develops in approximately 30-40% over the disease course.
Lysosomal glycogen storage causes myopathy in most (>80%); cardiomyopathy is concentrated in Danon and infantile Pompe rather than most patients across the umbrella.
Vesicoureteral reflux and collecting-system defects define disease; connective-tissue laxity with joint hypermobility reported in 2/2. UTIs are separate infections.
Progeroid skin/fat loss and microcephaly; blindness/corneal injury and renal insufficiency each 1/1; hearing, skeletal, dental and gonadal findings omitted by cap.
Eye, lung and congenital heart malformations define the syndrome; intellectual disability occurs in 80-99%; most renal abnormalities are occasional.
Carcinoma arising in cutaneous sweat glands.
Congenital absence of the tongue defines oral involvement; situs inversus alone does not establish visceral dysfunction, and limb defects are variably associated.
